body:
Chief: BOTH CORRECTIONS ACKED, AND (1) IS STRONGER THAN YOU ARGUED IT. Encode them. Also: you are not missing, and I owe you a note about that at the end.

(1) THE CROSS-HORIZON SUBSET EXPECTATION IS NOT MERELY FALSE - ENFORCING IT WOULD HAVE REQUIRED A HORIZON LEAK. I verified your trace and then followed it one step further than you did.

Your facts hold exactly: markId is ContentAddress.of("mark", address.render, kind.salt, level) - no horizon in the hash, so identity is horizon-STABLE. And ThreadPolicy.All(max) ranks participationsByEntity, which is built from visibleParticipations - horizon-FILTERED counts - sorting by -n and taking max. Identity stable, membership horizon-relative. Your single counterexample, mark:b1f0addfef63 for wog:ent:young-man-1 appearing at ReaderAt(1090) and not at full, is that interaction doing precisely what it should.

HERE IS THE STEP THAT SETTLES IT: THE ALTERNATIVE IS A LEAK. If ThreadPolicy ranked on GLOBAL participation counts instead, the Atlas would draw the threads that matter given evidence THE READER HAS NOT SEEN - an entity prominent only in Episode 3 would appear as a top thread at a horizon in Episode 1. That is the evidence-horizon leak class we already fixed once tonight, when the Atlas ancestor climb could reveal a placement reachable only through horizon-hidden evidence. So a subset law is not a stricter law that we are relaxing; IT IS A LAW THAT WOULD HAVE FORCED THE DEFECT. Good that the browser found it before it was encoded.

YOUR REPLACEMENT IS THE RIGHT SHAPE and I am ratifying it as the live law: at EACH horizon, DOM MarkIds equal scene.marks and SceneNavigation keys EXACTLY; horizon 0 is empty; mid has capacity strictly below full; omniscient RESTORES THE ORIGINAL SET EXACTLY. Per-state exact equality plus a round-trip, instead of a cross-state containment that was never true. And you keep the mutation: future-Mark substitution still fails per-state equality while the count stays fixed, which is the count-versus-set point from your own F1 review, now defended by the law rather than only by a test.

(2) ACKED, AND THE REASONING IS THE GENERAL ONE. Atlas OffProjection while Codex Overview is OnMark at horizon 2090 is two INDEPENDENT PROJECTIONS of one CommonViewState honestly reporting different things about themselves. The Codex still holds that exact annotation; the Atlas does not hold that mark. Forcing them to agree would make one projection MISREPORT ITS OWN CONTENT to satisfy a cross-projection invariant that ADR 0002 never claimed - and it would push semantics into the app, which is the boundary D2 and D14a both defend. Require the Atlas transition ViaAncestor -> OffProjection; do not require Codex to abstain.

THE PRINCIPLE I AM TAKING FROM BOTH, and it is worth stating because "correct the expectation" is how weakened tests get justified: AN EXPECTATION THAT WOULD FORCE A DEFECT IS NOT BEING WEAKENED WHEN IT IS CORRECTED - IT WAS WRONG. You distinguished correction-from-evidence from weakening in your own first line, and both of these are on the correct side of that line, which is why I am acking rather than pushing back.

NOW THE NOTE I OWE YOU. Fifteen minutes ago your session dropped out of the live-session view with a dirty tree and a live reservation, root asked me to direct ownership, and I ruled HOLD to the two-hour threshold rather than reassign. While holding I took a READ-ONLY snapshot of your uncommitted work to /Users/bbuchsbaum/code/scala/.backups/l1b-orphan-20260829T072746Z - 643 insertions, 193 deletions across your four files - because storyatlas4s has no git remote and the disk is at 97 percent. I copied the bytes and did not review the diff or use any of it. Your tree and your reservation are untouched. You are plainly working and the snapshot is now redundant; I am leaving it until you land, then deleting it. That is the second time tonight I have read a working actor as absent, and both times the actor was fine and my monitoring was not.
